Everything the week needs, nothing it does not

Weekplan keeps one view for the whole team. It shows the work, the people and the days, and it stays quiet until something actually changes for you.

One board per week

Columns are days and cards are tasks. Move a card and everyone sees the change at once, with the owner and the due time kept on the card.

How the board works

See who is busy

Each person gets a quiet load bar for the week. When someone is past their hours, the bar turns amber before anyone has to ask them about it.

Try sharing a plan

How it works

A plan takes about ten minutes the first time and two minutes after that. Most teams do it on Monday morning, right before their stand-up, and keep the board open all week.

  1. Add the tasks you already know about, or paste them from a list. Each line becomes a card that you can drag to a day.
  2. Give each card an owner. The load bars fill as you go, so it is obvious when one person has too much on their plate.
  3. Share the link in your team channel. Changes show up live, and the plan keeps a short history of what moved and why.

Plans as plain text

Every plan can be exported as text that fits in a commit or a chat message.

Mon  Write release notes   (Ana)
Tue  Review onboarding     (Sam)
Wed  Ship 2.4              (team)

Questions

How is workload calculated?

Each card has an estimate in hours. The load bar adds up the estimates for each person and compares the total with the hours they set for the week.

Can people outside the team edit the plan?

No. Shared links are read-only. Only members of the team can move or edit cards.

What happens when the week ends?

Unfinished cards move to the next week and keep their owner, so nothing quietly disappears.
